chapter: CBS, return to Ellington and retirement
title: Short-term trombonists of the 1960s
summary: Leon Cox, John Sanders, Benny Green as fourth trombone, and later men after he left in 1970.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: I see a trombone player here named Leon Cox who I've never heard of before. Who was he?
Leon was in there a very short time. And see, there's many of them that would come in, stay a short few weeks and then go. So --
(Inaudible) -- was there for a few months in '61 it says here.
Yes. Yeah he's -- went over to Harry James.
And you were never -- you were never in the band the same time that John Sanders was?
Right. Just for a short time. For a
few weeks. Yeah, I played with John. A very nice fellow. He's a father --
A priest.
-- a priest.
I saw him in the East.
Uh-huh.
Then in going on through the sixties, the trombone section was pretty stable there. It was you, and Chuck Connors, and Buster Cooper steadily through -- almost through the end of '69.
Yes.
And then -- oh then there was a period in '68 and '69 when Benny Green was the fourth trombone.
Right. Yes. Benny was there. Gee, you remind me of so many things.
How did you happen to get a fourth trombone?

Well, everyone was trying to build up, you know, and there were several bands that had 16, 17 men. And so, a fourth trombone became popular to everything. Made the -- enhanced the musical sounds. So, they got it. Benny was a very good man. Benny for a long time was in a small group. I forget the name of the group. It was very good. I think he's still down in Los Vegas.
Yeah, I think that's it. Then there
was a period -- Julian Priester -- for a minute it looks like and -- that was after -- right after you left, wasn't it?
Yes, that was in '70.
Yes.
Yeah.
And when you left Booty came back, is that right?
Yes, he came back for a while. Uh-huh.
But just for a while -- what '70 and '71.
Uh-huh.
And then Murray McEachern very briefly.
And --
Murry was there for quite a little while. I don't mean a year, but he was there for quite a few months.
And yes. I guess in '72 and into the beginning of '73.
Yes.
